title: Learning the Map
logline: Young novices memorise an ancient map of the mind, with 121 kinds of consciousness, by heart, long before they understand it.
human_question: What changes when you have a name for what is happening inside you?

premise.story: A term at a monastic school through one novice's routine: chanting, memorising, being tested, and ordinary childhood in between.
premise.experience: Rhythm of chanting, palm-leaf and exercise-book, the gap between reciting and understanding.

concept_links.why: The full map of consciousness as a thing that is learned, recited and carried.
How mind is classified by plane and kind.
The four ultimates as the frame of the map.

what_camera_could_observe: A teacher's question and a hesitant answer
what_must_be_real: The school's actual curriculum and the novices' own words. Consent from guardians and teachers.

possible_arc.opening: A child reciting words they cannot yet explain.
possible_arc.turn: A moment where a word meets their own experience, if it happens.
possible_arc.ending_open: The term ends; the map goes on.

requirements: A pirivena teaching Abhidhamma to young novices
Consent from guardians, teachers and the chief monk

suggestions.name: A village pirivena in the Kandy or Kegalle districts
suggestions.why: Many small monastic schools; hill landscape.
suggestions.verify: A specific school must be found and approached with care.

drop_if: The film can only work by explaining doctrine
unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: All content is editorial proposal. Location suggestions are AI suggestions only; selection belongs to Chathura.
